cues.text: A rocket engine carries its own fuel and oxygen.
That’s why it can work without air.
These pumps push the liquids down
making very hot gas under high pressure.
The gas flows through this narrow throat.
In the wider nozzle beyond it,
the gas expands and speeds up.
As the engine throws gas down,
the gas pushes the rocket up.
The engine turns stored chemical energy into motion.

provenance.transcript:
A rocket engine carries its own fuel and oxygen. That’s why it can work without air. These pumps push the liquids down into the chamber below. There, they mix and burn, making very hot gas under high pressure.

The gas flows through this narrow throat. In the wider nozzle beyond it, the gas expands and speeds up. As the engine throws gas down, the gas pushes the rocket up. The engine turns stored chemical energy into motion.
